elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Contractor to indemnify Company for IP claims but contains no duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Contractor must indemnify Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or Vendor breach-of-law trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The indemnity is limited to IP infringement or misappropriation claims and does not cover Contractor's breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or Contractor-caused data-breach trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The indemnity does not cover data breaches.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or gross-negligence trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: The indemnity does not cover gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or wilful-misconduct trigger is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The indemnity does not cover wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Vendor's defense protection must extend to Customer's affiliates for all covered claims.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation is provided, and affiliates are not identified as protected parties.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification protection must extend to Customer's affiliates for all covered claims.
elements.evidence: Only Company is indemnified; Company's affiliates are omitted.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the indemnified party to give notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no claim-notice procedure.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defense and settlement of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no defense-control or settlement-control provision.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from Customer or the other indemnified parties.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must be confined to claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No operative Company indemnity is included, so Company has no indemnity exposure outside the permitted categories; that is narrower than the stated limitation.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Contractor must indemnify Company against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes claims to the extent arising from Company's modification of the Services or Works.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Customer's combination of the Services or Deliverables with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes claims arising from Company's combination with items not supplied by Contractor.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer's specifications.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes claims arising from Contractor's compliance with Company's specifications.

elements.element: For an affected item, Vendor must have the remedy of procuring Customer's right to continue using it.
elements.evidence: Contractor may procure for Company the right to continue using the affected item.

elements.element: For an affected item, Vendor must have the remedy of modifying it.
elements.evidence: Contractor may modify the affected item.

elements.element: For an affected item, Vendor must have the remedy of replacing it.
elements.evidence: Contractor may replace the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor must refund the fees paid for the affected item if procurement, modification, and replacement are not reasonably available.
elements.evidence: If none of the preceding remedies is reasonably available, Contractor must refund the fees paid for the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor's aggregate liability for the IP indemnity must be capped at three times the annual fees.
elements.evidence: The indemnity paragraph states that Contractor's aggregate liability under Paragraph 7(d) shall not exceed three times the annual fees paid under the Agreement. The missing express '(d)' label is a drafting defect, but the paragraph's self-reference identifies the intended cap.

elements.element: The ordinary liability cap must not reduce the IP indemnity below the three-times-annual-fees super-cap.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 7(a) expressly carves Contractor's obligations under Paragraph 7(d) out of the ordinary fees-paid cap.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the fallback: it provides a third-party IP indemnity, all three stated exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and an effective 3× annual-fees super-cap. It does not reach preferred because it omits defense, affiliates, non-IP triggers, and indemnification procedures. The redline is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated terms because it adds an unrelated bilateral attorneys'-fees waiver, which may also impair recovery of enforcement or claim-related fees. Drafting is further weakened by malformed ordering, a second subsection (c), omission of an express (d) label despite repeated Paragraph 7(d) references, and a heading that still refers to indemnification of Contractor even though Contractor indemnifies Company.
